confirmed.title: A packet's accept_completion option merges the PR with no confirmation dialog
confirmed.claim: `DecisionPacket`'s "Confirm decision" button calls `onResolve(sel, note)` directly. When the selected option's `kind` is `accept_completion`, the page's `onResolve` posts `intent=resolve-packet`, and the server (`task-actions.server.ts:4170-4258`) runs the full acceptance contract including `attemptAcceptanceMerge` — a real, irreversible GitHub merge. No dialog is shown on this path: `AcceptConfirm` is wired only to the Current-state Accept button and the admin Force-accept (`task-detail-page.tsx:479`, `:462`). The only role guard here is `canResolveCompletion`; the button's visible label stays the generic "Confirm decision" and the accessible name is "Confirm decision: <option title>" — neither says a merge happens.
confirmed.canon: Ruling 20 (R15-1) / FR27: "Every accept passes a confirm dialog" stating what merges and any missing signals. Ruling 53 (R18-8/B1) extended the same requirement to the board drag AND the keyboard Move menu specifically because "the most irreversible action in the product was also its most casual one". `open_decision_packet` accepts all nine `PACKET_OPTION_KINDS` including `accept_completion` (operator-toolkit.server.ts:165), and `withdrawSupersededStuckPacket` (task-actions.server.ts:1722, :1743) explicitly special-cases accept_completion-bearing packets, so this is a live, expected packet shape — not a theoretical one.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An operator opens a decision packet on VIB-7 whose options include `accept_completion` ("Accept the completion and close it"), pre-selected as the operator pick so `sel` already points at it on first paint. A maintainer opens the task, reads the packet, and presses "Confirm decision" — one click, no dialog. Viberr merges PR #147 into `main` and moves VIB-7 to Done. The user never saw the PR number, the delivered revision sha, the verdict state, or the merge target, and had no "Not yet" to press; the identical action from the board or the Current-state panel would have shown all four.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: resolving a decision packet's `accept_completion` option performs the same irreversible PR merge as the Accept button, but its two-step confirm (radiogroup + "Confirm decision", decision-packet.tsx:317-338) never states the merge — no PR number, no delivered revision sha, no verdict/missing-signal line, no merge target, and no wording that merging is one-way. It renders only the operator's freeform title/body/observations, which may legitimately be empty (operator-actions.server.ts:780 maps only what the operator supplied), and the option's own copy is whatever the operator typed. That contradicts FR27/ruling 20's requirement that every acceptance pass a confirmation "stating what will merge and naming any missing signals", and it is the un-shipped half of pass 18's B1 remedy (GAP-ANALYSIS.md:223-224) — ruling 53 closed only the board drag and keyboard Move menu. The concrete defect is the ABSENT MERGE DISCLOSURE on an existing confirm step, not an absent confirm step. Concrete scenario: operator opens a completion packet on VIB-7 with observations `Changed: 9 files` and `Validation: green` and an `accept_completion` option titled "Accept the completion and close it" marked recommended; a maintainer presses the pre-selected "Confirm decision" and PR #147 merges into main — the same action from the Current-state panel would first have shown PR #147, head sha, the reviewer verdict, `main` as the target, and a "Not yet" escape. (Note: the sibling `accept_completion` recommendation Apply button, operator-recommendations.tsx:101-110 -> task-actions.server.ts:5549, has the same gap and no confirm step at all — that one WAS in the three R18-7 was meant to cover and is arguably the stronger finding.)

Two precisions to the claim, neither of which defeats it. (1) The packet path is not gate-free server-side: `resolvePacket` re-runs `requireAcceptCompletion`, `acceptanceRefusalReason` (verdict/R15-1, closed-PR/D-4, graph position) and `acceptancePrHeadCheck` before merging (`task-actions.server.ts:4170-4210`). What is missing is specifically the R15-1 CONFIRM DIALOG and its disclosure (PR number, delivered head sha, verdict state, target branch) plus a "Not yet" escape — so the defect is one-click irreversible merge without disclosure, not an ungated merge. (2) `canResolveCompletion` in the page is `canDecideOwned` (maintainer+ OR the contributor-owner, R6-2/R14-2), so the unconfirmed one-click merge is reachable by a contributor who owns the task as well as by maintainers/admins. Worth noting alongside: `open_packet` accepts `accept_completion` as an option kind even for an operator without the `completion-for-acceptance` grant, which is what makes the state easy to reach.

confirmed.title: Archived board cards render live readiness/validation/waiting pills and full move controls, directly under a banner saying they are out of the flow
confirmed.claim: Under the `archived` board filter, `matchesBoardFilter` (board-filters.ts:36) returns archived tasks and `StageBoard` renders them through the ordinary `TaskCard`. The card draws `<ReadinessPill value={task.displayReadiness}/>` (:257), `<ValidationPill value={task.validation}/>` (:331) and `<WaitTag/>` (:334, "waiting on a human"), and carries the drag surface plus the `StageMenu` move control (:340-348) whenever `canTransition`. Nothing on the card marks it archived — there is no archived class, pill, or CSS treatment (`grep archiv app/app.css` yields only `.archived-banner` for archived PROJECTS and `.archive-hint`). Three lines above, the page renders `role="status"`: "Archived tasks — abandoned work kept for the record… they are out of the review queue" (:1362-1369).
confirmed.canon: Ruling 16/R14-3 and UXO-1 (this pass, `d69af18`): `TaskHero` now renders the readiness pill and `ValidationPill` only when `!archived`, because "a task archived mid-review still read 'ready · awaiting verdict', i.e. that someone still owes a verdict, when nobody does". The UX spec's State Semantics rule — "Every state must mean the same thing everywhere it appears" — makes the board the same contract as detail. `transitionStage`/`reorderTask` also carry no archived guard, so the offered move control actually fires a governed transition on an archived task (only `acceptCompletion` checks `archivedTaskBlockedReason`).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A maintainer archives VIB-12 while it sits in Review awaiting a verdict, then clicks the board's "Archived · 1" chip. The Review column shows VIB-12's card reading "ready · awaiting verdict · waiting on a human" with a working Move-to-stage menu — the exact string UXO-1 removed from the task page one commit earlier — while the banner directly above it says this work is abandoned and out of the review queue. Opening the task shows "archived" and no live pills. The two surfaces describe the same task with opposite vocabularies at the same instant.
corrections: Under the board's Archived filter, TaskCard (app/features/board/board-page.tsx:257, :331) and the ListView row (:512) still render the live ReadinessPill and ValidationPill with no archived marker on the card itself and no archived CSS treatment — so a task archived mid-review reads "ready · awaiting verdict", the exact assertion UXO-1 (d69af18) deliberately removed from TaskHero because an archived task owes nobody a verdict, directly under a role="status" banner (:1362-1369) saying the work is abandoned and out of the review queue. Drop the "waiting on a human" element: archiving sets waiting="none" and withdraws the packet (task-actions.server.ts:4046-4048), so WaitTag never renders. Separately (and arguably the stronger half): for admin/maintainer viewers the archived card keeps a working drag surface and StageMenu (:340-348), and neither transitionStage (:2998) nor reorderTask (:3879) checks archivedTaskBlockedReason — a move to any non-final stage succeeds and fires autoInvokeOperator (:3242), which has no archived gate, re-engaging the operator on abandoned work. Only the move into the final stage is blocked, via acceptCompletion (:4741). Neither the board pills nor the transition gap has any test coverage (board-page.test.tsx has zero occurrences of "archived").

One element of the stated failure string does not reproduce: `setTaskArchived` forces `frontmatter.waiting = "none"` (task-actions.server.ts:4042), so `WaitTag` (board-page.tsx:128-148) returns null and "waiting on a human" is NOT drawn on a card archived through the app. The accurate narrower claim: under the Archived filter the card renders a live `ReadinessPill` and `ValidationPill` (e.g. "ready · awaiting verdict"), plus a draggable wrapper and a working `StageMenu`, with nothing marking it archived — directly under the banner saying the work is abandoned and out of the review queue, and contradicting the task page, which since commit d69af18 (UXO-1) suppresses exactly those two pills for archived tasks. ("waiting on a human" can still appear afterwards, since moving the archived card re-triggers the operator and re-sets `waiting`, but that is a second-order consequence, not the first-render state.)

confirmed.title: Rail Board and Review badges count archived tasks; the board header and the review queue exclude them
confirmed.claim: `tasks` (:109) is flattened from `getBoard`, which loads with `includeArchived: true` (board-query.server.ts:202-204). `taskCount: tasks.length` (:116) feeds the rail's Board badge and `reviewCount` (:117-124) counts `tasks.filter(t => t.stage === reviewId)` — both include archived tasks. The board header computes its own count from `liveTasks = allTasks.filter(t => !isArchived(t))` (board-page.tsx:1243, :1336), and `getReviewQueue` goes through the default `listProjectTasks` which appends `AND archived = 0` (board-query.server.ts:164), so the queue's rows and its `total` exclude them.
confirmed.canon: Ruling 16/R14-3: archived tasks "leave the board's default view and the review queue". `review-queue.server.ts:19-22` states the parity contract explicitly — the queue's qualification "is the exact predicate the workspace-layout rail badge uses (routes/project.tsx), so the two counts can never drift" — and cites the pass-4 WI-1 regression that came from exactly this drift. The UX spec's Navigation/State rules require the same state to read the same everywhere.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A project has 3 tasks, one of which (in Review) is archived. The left rail reads "Board 3" and "Review queue 1"; clicking Board shows a header reading "2 tasks · 0 waiting on a human decision" over columns holding two cards, and clicking Review queue shows "0 tasks at the review boundary" with both panels empty. A supervisor chasing the rail's "1" finds nothing and cannot tell whether the queue is broken or the badge is.
corrections: Real, with two halves of unequal strength — file it with the review badge as the head. HARD contradiction: the rail's Review badge (project.tsx:117-124) counts archived review-stage tasks while getReviewQueue excludes them, directly contradicting R14-3's "archived tasks leave ... the review queue" and the archive event's own copy at task-actions.server.ts:4030, and falsifying the parity contract asserted at review-queue.server.ts:16-17 (the claim cited :19-22; the comment is actually at :16-17). SOFTER half: the rail's Board badge vs the board header (rail 3 / header 2) is a cross-surface disagreement rather than a ruling violation — "total incl. archived" is a defensible reading of the badge, and the comments at project.tsx:36 and rail.tsx:6-8 cite ruling 16 for "ALL tasks incl. Done", which does not cover the archived axis either way. The fix for the Board badge is arguably a doc/label correction; the fix for the Review badge is code (exclude archived, restoring the stated parity). Also worth noting: neither count has any test with an archived task.

Scope note: the Board badge's inclusion of Done tasks is deliberate (ruling 16) — only the inclusion of ARCHIVED tasks in both rail badges is the defect. Also, the review-page mismatch is the sharper half: the rail's Review badge counts a stage-filtered set that still contains archived tasks, while the review queue drops them, so the two numbers disagree with no way for the user to reconcile them.

confirmed.title: "Complete merge" is hidden from the contributor-owner the server authorizes, stranding a merge-pending PR
confirmed.claim: `useRunControls` gates the merge-completion affordance on `roleCan(myRole, "accept-completion")` alone; `accept-completion` is `[admin, maintainer]` (rbac.ts:68). When it is false, `onCompleteMerge` is `undefined` and `GithubTrace` never renders the "Complete merge" button (task-side-panels.tsx:221). The server's `completeTaskMerge` calls `requireAcceptCompletion(db, project, actor, fm.ownerUserId, …)` (task-actions.server.ts:5346), which short-circuits on `ownerException` — so a contributor who owns the task IS authorized. Every neighbouring surface on the same page already carries that exception: `acceptance.hasAuthority` (server-resolved), `canDecideOwned` (task-detail-page.tsx:202), `canResolveCompletion`, and the Permissions panel row (task-side-panels.tsx:303-305).
confirmed.canon: Ruling 22 (R14-2, widening R6-2): "the owner governs any open decision on their own task". Ruling 40 (R16-6): an operator acceptance records the PR `accepted` (merge pending) and "a human completes the merge later". P14-GV-04 in this very file's neighbour fixed the identical defect for the Permissions panel; E3's rule is to ask for the action the SERVER enforces.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A full-autonomy operator with `completion-for-acceptance: direct` accepts VIB-9. The PR is recorded `accepted` and the task moves to Done. Arda, a contributor who holds VIB-9's owner seat, opens the task: the GitHub panel shows the amber "PR #147 · merge pending" pill, the Permissions panel tells him "You own this task — you can accept it → Done", and there is no control anywhere on the page to finish the merge. The one action the state is waiting for is invisible to the exact person the server would let perform it.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the client-side gate on the "Complete merge" button is stricter than the server gate it fronts. `task-detail-hooks.ts:116` asks `roleCan(myRole, "accept-completion")` while `completeTaskMerge` authorizes maintainer+ OR the task's live contributor owner (owner exception, R6-2, pinned by policy-rbac.server.test.ts:316), so a contributor-owner is denied an action the server would allow — the same class of defect P14-GV-04 fixed for the Permissions panel and R15-2's canDeliver already handles correctly. The visible harm is an honesty contradiction, not a hard strand: the merge-pending nudge is delivered to that owner (notifyTaskWatchers includes ownerUserId) and tells them to use "the task's Complete-merge button", which never renders for them; the PR remains completable by any maintainer/admin in-app or by the owner on GitHub, so "the one action the state is waiting for is invisible to the exact person the server would let perform it" is right, but "stranding a merge-pending PR" is not. Two secondary inaccuracies: the ruling citation should be FR37/R14-2/R6-2 plus ruling 40 (INTENT ruling 22 is R15-3, not R14-2), and the quoted Permissions-panel line concerns accept → Done, which on an already-Done task is separately denied by resolveAcceptanceAffordance's terminal-stage early return. Also worth fixing alongside: the stale "admin|maintainer only" comments at task-detail-hooks.ts:115 and routes/project.task.tsx:421 misstate the server gate, and no test covers the client visibility of this button.

One nuance worth carrying into the write-up: the owner is not absolutely stranded — the same notification also offers "or via GitHub", and a maintainer/admin can still press the button, so the defect is an in-app affordance/authority mismatch (UI narrower than the server it calls, and narrower than the copy on the same page) rather than a state that can never be resolved by anyone.

confirmed.title: The execution profile says an unowned task is "open to any project member" next to a sibling line saying contributor-or-above only
confirmed.claim: The "Human owner" cell renders `{!o && Unowned — open to any project member}` unconditionally, then renders `` in the same `.rev-row`. For a viewer, `OwnerControl` takes its `!o && !canOwn` branch and renders `Unowned — a contributor or above can take it` (:121). Both strings therefore paint side by side in one row. `own-task` is `[admin, maintainer, contributor]` (rbac.ts:65) and `setOwner` enforces it, so the first sentence is false for viewers regardless of who is reading.
confirmed.canon: Ruling 2 (amended) / Q5 clean tiering — project roles are a strict 4-tier and only contributor+ may hold the owner seat; the same page's Permissions panel renders the matrix truth ("Task ownership: View only — contributor+ to own", task-side-panels.tsx:296). The UX spec's consistency rule: "Every repeated state must mean the same thing everywhere", and the honesty rule that a surface whose job is stating what the server enforces must not carry aspirational copy.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A project Viewer opens an unowned task VIB-3. The Execution profile's Human-owner row reads: "Unowned — open to any project member    Unowned — a contributor or above can take it" — two contradictory sentences touching each other — while the Permissions panel below says "View only — contributor+ to own" and the Current-state panel just says "Unowned" with no control. The reader cannot tell whether they may take the task.
corrections: Real, but narrow it on two points. (a) The literal two-contradictory-sentences-touching render happens only for roles that cannot own (viewer); for contributor+ the same unguarded line paints next to the "Assign me" button, which is an honesty defect but not a visible self-contradiction. (b) The sharper statement of the defect is that "Unowned — open to any project member" (execution-profile.tsx:802) is false for EVERY reader, not just viewers — viewers are project members and `own-task` excludes them (rbac.ts:65, enforced in setOwner) — so the line is unconditionally aspirational copy on a surface whose job is stating what the server enforces, and it additionally duplicates/contradicts OwnerControl's own unowned-state sentence at :121 when the reader is a viewer.

Accurate narrower claim: execution-profile.tsx:802 hardcodes "Unowned — open to any project member", which is false because `own-task` excludes viewers (rbac.ts:65) and `setOwner` enforces it (task-actions.server.ts:~2868, "Ownership can only be handed to a project member who can own tasks (contributor or above)"). The two-sentences-touching rendering is specifically reproduced when the reader lacks `own-task` (project viewer, or any member whose role fails `roleCan(myRole,"own-task")`) AND the task is unowned; for contributor/maintainer/admin readers the same false sentence renders next to the "Assign me" button instead, so it is a copy-honesty defect for everyone and a contradictory-adjacent-copy defect for viewers only.

confirmed.title: Retired "primary specialist" vocabulary is still rendered in recommendation labels, the @-mention picker and timeline events
confirmed.claim: `operatorAssignSpecialist` writes the recommendation label `Assign ${name} as the primary specialist` (:1280) and `operatorRunSpecialist` writes `Start the primary specialist's run` (:1312). These labels pass through the loader verbatim (`project.task.tsx:191` → `recommendations`) into `.op-rec-title` (operator-recommendations.tsx:92). Two other rendered sites carry the same dead word: the @-mention autocomplete row for `@agent` has sub-label "Primary specialist" (mention-suggestions.server.ts:64 → mention-autocomplete.ts:55 `sub: r.label`), and the deployment timeline event reads "Deployed **X** … as the primary specialist" (specialist-run.server.ts:391).
confirmed.canon: FR14 amendment 2026-08-04 (pass 17, D9/Q17-5): "vocabulary re-synced — 'primary specialist'/'consultant specialists' no longer exist"; INTENT §6 divergence 5 calls it "dead vocabulary". UXA-6 (this pass, `6ba5c77`) renamed `KIND_LABEL.assign_specialist` to "Delivering agent" for precisely this reason — "the same actor wore two names one viewport apart" — but changed only the kind label, not the recommendation's own label rendered beside it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A supervised operator recommends a deliverer. The card renders as "⟨branch icon⟩ Delivering agent — Assign Codex Developer as the primary specialist" — the kind label and the title of the SAME card naming the same actor two different things. One panel below, the Execution profile cell is headed "Delivering agent", the assign menu says "Assign delivering agent", and typing `@` in the comment box offers `@agent · Primary specialist`. Three names for one role on one screen.
corrections: Real, and if anything understated — but tighten the framing from "FR14 amendment violated" to the on-screen contradiction, which is what a user actually hits. Narrow accurate claim: UXA-6's fix was incomplete. Under a SUPERVISED operator, one recommendation card renders kind label "Delivering agent" (operator-recommendations.tsx:46) directly beside its own title "Assign Codex Developer as the primary specialist" (operator-actions.server.ts:1280 -> :92), and the run card reads "Run specialist — Start the primary specialist's run" (:48 / :1312). Same page, the @-mention picker offers "@agent · Primary specialist" (mention-suggestions.server.ts:64 -> mention-menu.tsx:100) while the execution profile says "Delivering agent" / "Assign delivering agent" (execution-profile.tsx:671, :287). Two additions the claim missed: (1) app/shared/capabilities.ts:35 renders a fourth site, cap("assign-primary-specialist", "Assign the primary specialist"), visible on the Agents page and asserted by agents-page.test.tsx:656 — so the sweep also has to decide whether the capability's DISPLAY label follows (the capability id itself is machinery and can stay); (2) UXA-6 explicitly prescribed run_specialist -> "Run delivering agent" and that half was never applied. Lower-severity within the finding: specialist-run.server.ts:391 is a past-tense historical timeline record rather than a live control, so it is the least user-confusing of the sites (though its test at :236 pins the retired word and would need updating).

Two refinements. (a) The recommendation-card surfaces are conditional: they only appear when the operator's assign-primary-specialist capability is set to `recommend` (catalog default is `direct`, in which case the action is performed and no card is written) and autonomy is below `full`; the mention-picker sub-label and the assignment timeline event are unconditional and need no configuration. (b) The on-card contradiction is slightly wider than stated: KIND_LABEL.run_specialist is still "Run specialist" (operator-recommendations.tsx:48) — only assign_specialist was renamed to "Delivering agent" — so pass-18 UXA-6's own prescribed sweep is itself half-applied. A fix must also update the three tests that currently assert the retired copy.

confirmed.title: The board's List view drops the merge-pending / closed-PR pills the card carries, re-opening the H10 defect in one of two board views
confirmed.claim: `ListView`'s row renders key, title, StageMenu, owner, reviewer stack, `ReadinessPill`, `ValidationPill` and `WaitTag` (:486-519). It renders no PR chip at all, so the `prStatePill` block that `TaskCard` renders for `pr.state === "accepted" | "closed"` (:303-307), the failing-checks pill (:312) and the `changes_requested` pill (:319) have no equivalent. Both views are the same board, toggled by `?view=list`.
confirmed.canon: Ruling 40 (R16-6): the merge-pending vs merged difference "must be visible where the task lives (board card and review queue), not only on the detail page". The card's own comment (:281-302) records the closed-PR half as live finding H10: "closing PR #124 unmerged produced a decision packet, a 'PR closed' badge and a divergence notification on the DETAIL page, while the card still read 'ready · awaiting verdict'".
confirmed.failure_scenario: A teammate closes PR #124 unmerged on GitHub. In Board view the VIB-4 card shows a rose "closed" pill and matches the "Blocked or waiting" filter. The supervisor toggles to List — the same task now reads "ready · awaiting verdict" with no PR signal at all, exactly the H10 state, and the two views of the same board disagree about whether VIB-4 needs a human.
corrections: Real but overstated. Accurate narrower claim: the board's List view (board-page.tsx:459-525) renders NO PR-derived signal at all — no #N chip, no prStatePill for `accepted` (merge pending) or `closed`, no failing-checks pill, no changes_requested pill — while the grid card renders all of them (:266-323) and the "Blocked or waiting" filter selects on pr.state === "closed" (board-filters.ts:59). This is the same parity gap P13-D-6 closed for ValidationPill in both views, and it has no list-view test (board-page.test.tsx:544-587 only exercises the grid). Two corrections to the framing: (1) it is an OMISSION, not a contradiction — `waiting`/`waitingOnMe` are untouched by the closed-PR reconcile path (github-reconciler.server.ts sets only pr/github plus timeline, notification and superseded recs), so the list row still draws its WaitTag and the two views do not disagree about whether a human is needed; the list simply omits WHICH decision is pending. So it is not "exactly the H10 state". (2) R16-6's letter names "board card and review queue", and the implementation record (planning/discovery-2026-08-04/IMPLEMENTATION.md:197-208) enumerates the surfaces actually covered as board card + task detail + GitHub view, with the review-queue half declared structurally out of scope. The list view is an unconsidered surface rather than one a ruling explicitly demanded — so this is a medium-severity parity/coverage gap against the spirit of ruling 40 and the P13-D-6 precedent, not a re-opened H10.

Two details in the claim's failure scenario should be tightened. (1) The list row drops MORE than the pills: it renders no PR number chip and no branch chip either, so the list shows literally zero PR information, not just a missing pill. (2) "the same task now reads 'ready · awaiting verdict' with no PR signal at all" is only exactly true in the window before the `pr-diverged` operator trigger opens its recovery packet; once that packet sets `waiting: "human"` (operator-actions.server.ts:561/795), the list row's WaitTag will read "waiting on a human"/"waiting on you". The defect is still real in both windows — the list never says the PR was closed (or is merge-pending) — so the accurate narrower claim is "the list view carries no PR-state signal", not "the list view shows no human-attention signal".

confirmed.title: The accept-completion dialog prints the raw internal PR state token instead of the canonical pill label
confirmed.claim: The "Merges" row renders `PR #{task.pr.number} · {task.pr.state}` — the raw `PR_STATE_VALUES` enum member (`review | merged | closed | accepted`, task-file.schema.ts:249). Every other surface routes PR state through `prStatePill` (github-pills.ts:44-50), which maps those tokens to "in review", "merged", "closed", "merge pending": the task-detail GitHub bar (task-side-panels.tsx:128), the board card (:304), the review queue (review-page.tsx:63), the GitHub page PR list and branch table.
confirmed.canon: Ruling 12 plus ruling 14's "shared single implementations… never fork per surface". UI-36 fixed this exact class on task detail and UXA-2 (this pass, `7ee2864`) fixed it again on the review queue, whose comment names the rule: the queue "carried its OWN pr-state colour map… Use the one map." The UX spec's State Semantics rule requires one vocabulary per state on every surface.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A maintainer opens the accept dialog for VIB-9. Behind the dialog the GitHub panel's pill reads "PR #147 · in review"; inside the dialog the Merges row reads "PR #147 · review". The dialog that exists to state precisely what is about to merge is the one place in the app that speaks the database's vocabulary instead of the product's.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the two task dialogs — accept-confirm.tsx:78-82 AND archive-confirm.tsx:80-87 (which does the same, `PR #{n} {state}`, no separator) — are the surfaces that bypass `prStatePill`. It is not "the one place in the app". The user-visible *text* difference is limited to `review` → canonical "in review" (and the rarely-reachable `accepted` → "merge pending"); `merged` and `closed` produce identical labels either way. The more consequential half is the hardcoded `kind="neutral"`: a closed-unmerged PR renders as neutral informational chrome in the dialogs that merge/archive it, where every other surface renders it `risk` — the exact UI-36 / UXA-2 defect class named in the comments at task-side-panels.tsx:123-127 and review-page.tsx:56-61. Fix is one line per dialog: use `prStatePill(task.pr.state)` for both kind and label. Severity: low (cosmetic vocabulary/tone drift in a high-stakes dialog), not a correctness or honesty failure — every load-bearing fact in the dialog (PR number, revision, drift, verdict, target branch) is accurate.

Claim is accurate; one addition — besides the label, the dialog also hardcodes Pill kind="neutral" instead of prStatePill's kind (info/done/risk/input), so the pill tone diverges from every sibling surface as well, and the "accepted" state (full-autonomy tasks) is the more misleading instance than "review".

confirmed.title: Any second run on a task strips the .claude catalog out from under a live Claude run, silently unmounting its granted skills (Claude runs only)
confirmed.claim: The workspace clone is per-TASK (`<taskDir>/workspace/<repo>`, specialist-run.server.ts:1854-1857), shared by every engagement. `cloneRepo`'s reuse path calls `stripUngovernedRepoCatalog(dir)` unconditionally on every run (:1868), and `mountGrantedSkills` calls it again itself (skill-mount.server.ts:166) and `rmSync`s the whole `.claude` when nothing mounts (:177-180). The server-side single-flight guard only covers the DELIVERING engagement (specialist-run.server.ts:684-701) — the comment at :682 states supporting agents 'run concurrently'. So a second run started while a Claude run is streaming deletes that run's `<workspace>/.claude/skills/*` and replaces them with its own (or with nothing). The live run was launched with `settingSources: ['project']` + `skills: [<its own names>]` (claude-runtime.server.ts:607-608) and its persona deliberately did NOT inject those skill bodies (specialist-run.server.ts:1233-1253, 'invoke one by name and its full instructions load then'), so the bodies exist nowhere else. There is no lock, no ref-count, and no test covering two concurrent mounts (skill-mount.server.test.ts only tests sequential re-mount at :320).
confirmed.canon: decisions.md ruling 51 (R18-5) — 'granted skills reach a Claude run through the SDK's NATIVE skills: progressive disclosure'; skill-mount.server.ts:20-41 docstring — 'after mountGrantedSkills returns, the workspace's .claude holds Viberr content or nothing, unconditionally'; the codebase's standing silent-resource rule (C1, specialist-run.server.ts:1341-1357: a grant that does not reach the run must be named in the prompt).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Task VIB-1 on a repo project. Delivering profile `dev` (Claude) is granted skill `conventional-commits`; supporting profile `qa` is granted skill `test-standards`. `dev`'s run starts: cloneRepo strips, mountGrantedSkills writes `.claude/skills/conventional-commits`, the SDK starts with `skills: ['conventional-commits']` and the persona says the skill is installed but omits its body. corrections: Narrower accurate claim: a second specialist run started on a task while a Claude run with mounted skills is still streaming deletes that live run's <workspace>/.claude and replaces it with the second run's set (or nothing), because the workspace is per-task and cloneRepo's reuse path strips unconditionally (specialist-run.server.ts:1868) with no lock or ref-count. Two corrections to the write-up: (1) mountGrantedSkills does NOT always strip — it returns early at skill-mount.server.ts:152-153 when the second run has zero granted skills — but cloneRepo:1868 strips regardless of backend or grants, so the wipe still occurs for a Codex or skill-less second run; (2) actual capability loss requires the first run to invoke a Skill AFTER the wipe, and a second run by the same profile with identical grants re-mounts byte-identical content, leaving only a brief window where the folder is absent. So the defect is a real unguarded race with a timing-dependent blast radius, not a guaranteed loss on every second run.

Accurate as filed, with one narrowing: it is a race window rather than a deterministic failure on every second run. The delivering run only observes the loss if it invokes a skill (or the SDK re-reads the project setting source) AFTER the second run's strip lands; its already-loaded name+description metadata keeps advertising the skill regardless, which is what makes the failure silent. Also worth stating precisely: the second run does not need to be a fresh run — the resume path re-mounts into the same shared clone via resolveResumeConfinement (specialist-run.server.ts:1685-1697), so an @mention that RESUMES a supporting agent wipes the live run's catalog too.

confirmed.title: The Claude-vs-Codex skills asymmetry required by R18-5 is disclosed nowhere in rendered UI — the same skill grant is whole on Claude and budget-clipped on Codex
confirmed.claim: The 'What differs between the two runtimes' list is the product's only rendered disclosure of backend differences. It enumerates seven items (coding harness, mid-run comments, ask-human timing, MCP credentials, MCP tool names, MCP not gated by the matrix, operator web egress) and says nothing about skills. Meanwhile the carriers genuinely differ: a Claude run that mounts gets each granted skill's full folder via the SDK and spends none of the injection budget (specialist-run.server.ts:1233-1258), while a Codex run always takes the prompt-text path through `readSkillBodies` under a shared 24 000-char budget (skill-body.server.ts:36, 224-241) that CLIPS a long skill (:191-198) or omits it entirely once the budget is spent (:176-189). The Agents page renders one identical `ResGroup label="Skills"` chip list for every profile regardless of backend (agents-page.tsx:722). No rendered string anywhere in app/features, app/routes or app/ui mentions native vs prompt-text skill delivery.
confirmed.canon: decisions.md ruling 51 (R18-5): 'Codex keeps prompt-text injection — the asymmetry is disclosed, not silent.' INTENT.md §6 deliberate divergence 18: 'native SDK skills for Claude, prompt-text injection for Codex; disclosed, not hidden.'
confirmed.failure_scenario: An admin attaches a 40 000-char `terraform-review` skill to two profiles, `dev-claude` (Claude) and `dev-codex` (Codex), and both show the identical `terraform-review` chip under Context resources. The Claude run receives the whole skill on invocation. The Codex run receives the first 24 000 chars with a truncation marker, and if a second skill is also granted, that second skill is omitted entirely. The admin who compares the two runs' output has no surface anywhere in the app that explains why the Codex agent ignored the checklist in the second half of the skill — the only explanation lives in server-side code comments.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the capability matrix modal's "What differs between the two runtimes" list (app/features/agents/capability-matrix-modal.tsx:194-241) — the product's only rendered disclosure of backend asymmetry, and the surface R18-5's "disclosed, not silent" points at — omits the R18-5 skills carrier difference entirely, and no other rendered string in app/features, app/routes or app/ui mentions it. The real discriminator is MOUNTED vs INJECTED, not Claude vs Codex: a mounted skill (Claude + a plain git checkout + an SDK-acceptable name) arrives whole and spends none of the budget, while every other grant — every Codex run, any Claude run without a checkout, and any single skill that fails to mount — rides the prompt under the shared 24 000-char budget and is clipped or dropped. The genuinely silent case is CLIPPING: `skill-body.server.ts:191-198` truncates with a marker inside the prompt but records no `UnresolvedSkillGrant`, so nothing outside the model's own context knows. Full OMISSION is already half-disclosed — it emits an unresolved grant that the persona surfaces to the agent with an instruction to report it (specialist-run.server.ts:1347-1357) — though that channel is model-mediated and still has no rendered surface (no per-run "granted but did not reach this run" UI). Fix is a bullet in the runtime-differences list (plus, ideally, surfacing `skillSet.unresolved` and the clip on the run/agent surface), not a code-behavior change.

Two narrowings. (1) The FULLY-OMITTED skill is not completely silent: specialist-run.server.ts:1347-1357 lists it in the run prompt under "Attached resources that did NOT reach this run" and instructs the agent to state it in its reply, so a human can learn of it second-hand through the agent's report. The CLIPPED skill (skill-body.server.ts:191-198) is genuinely silent outside server logs — that is the sharp end of the finding. (2) The split is per-RUN, not strictly per-backend: mountGrantedSkills requires backend === "claude" AND realBackend AND a checkout dir, so a Claude run without a workspace also falls back to budget-clipped prompt-text injection. Any disclosure copy should say "mounted natively on a Claude run with a workspace; otherwise injected as prompt text under a shared 24,000-char budget that clips or drops long skills" rather than framing it as Claude-always-native.

confirmed.title: runbook.md claims expired sessions are "swept at boot and daily" from a table named `sessions`; neither the sweep nor the table exists
confirmed.claim: The Auth/access runbook section states: "Sessions live in SQLite (`sessions`); expired sessions are swept at boot and daily." (a) The table is `session` (singular, better-auth-owned, camelCase columns) — `db/migrations/0001_baseline.sql` creates `"session"`; there is no `sessions` table anywhere in the baseline. (b) `bootServer()` (app/server/boot.server.ts:180-317) runs dirs → writer lock → lock guard → agent assets → seed admin → event publisher → boot rescan → base agents → file watcher → KB watcher → `finalizeOrphanedRuns` → `applyRetention` → `reconcileRestartedWork` → `startScheduleRunner` → `startGithubReconcilePoller`. No session sweep. `applyRetention` (app/server/db/retention.server.ts:59-102) touches only `run_log_lines`, `audit_events` and `notifications`. There is no daily timer: better-auth is configured with only `session.expiresIn`/`updateAge` (app/lib/auth.server.ts:247-250). Expired rows are deleted lazily, one at a time, when a request happens to present one (app/server/auth/require-user.server.ts:89).
confirmed.canon: docs/architecture/decisions.md ruling 44 / R17-3 — `runbook.md` is named as a required re-read target every pass, because "a correct change elsewhere" leaves operational statements stale. FR33/NFR18 (durable, bounded audit and app state) and the runbook's own "Retention & growth" section, which enumerates every retained table and its policy.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An operator investigating SQLite file growth on a long-lived instance opens the runbook, reads that sessions are swept daily, and rules session rows out. They then run `SELECT count(*) FROM sessions` to confirm and get `no such table: sessions`, concluding their database is corrupt or the schema drifted. In reality `session` grows monotonically for any user who never returns after a sign-in (30-day `expiresIn` rows are only deleted if that exact session is presented again after expiry), and no documented pruning path exists.
corrections: Two canon docs assert a session sweep that does not exist, and the runbook additionally names a table that does not exist. docs/operations/runbook.md:92 says "Sessions live in SQLite (`sessions`); expired sessions are swept at boot and daily" and planning/planning-artifacts/architecture.md:309 says "Expired sessions are swept at boot and daily". The table is `session` (db/migrations/0001_baseline.sql:339); no boot sweep exists (app/server/db/retention.server.ts:59-102 covers only run_log_lines, audit_events, notifications) and no periodic timer exists (app/lib/auth.server.ts:247-250 configures only expiresIn/updateAge). Expired rows are removed only opportunistically by better-auth when that exact token is presented after expiry (node_modules/better-auth/dist/api/routes/session.mjs:182-189), so `session` grows unbounded for users who never return. Contradicted canon is ruling 44 / R17-3 (operational docs must be re-read against the tree each pass) plus the runbook's own "Retention & growth" table, which enumerates every retained table and its policy — not FR33/NFR18, which bound audit retention. Correct fix is documentation in both files (or, if unbounded session growth is deemed unacceptable, add the sweep the docs already promise).

Sound as a docs-honesty finding, not as a triggerable app defect: there is no UI action or agent tool call that reaches this text, so the only "reproduction" is an operator reading a linked doc. Drop the speculative "concludes their database is corrupt" step — the verifiable harm is simply that the runbook names a table that does not exist and promises a boot+daily sweep that no code performs, while `session` rows for users who never return are pruned only if that same session is later presented after its 30-day expiry. The fix is wider than one line: docs/architecture/decisions.md:51 repeats the same stale plural `sessions` in the naming-convention ruling (better-auth owns singular camelCase `session`/`user`, an unrecorded exception), and README.md:243-244 claims `provenance` is "the one table with no retention", which the same evidence contradicts.

confirmed.title: A failed delivery push records its reason nowhere — not in the timeline, not in the log
confirmed.claim: `pushWorkspaceBranch` classifies git's stderr only for the non-fast-forward case (`isNonFastForwardStderr`, :378). Every other push failure takes the branch at :391-402: the log line deliberately omits stderr ("Redact stderr — a git push failure can echo the remote URL/token") and the returned reason is the literal string `"git push returned non-zero"`. `performDelivery` (app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts:3429-3442) interpolates that string straight into the human-visible timeline event and the typed outcome: "VIB-1's execution branch could not be pushed (git push returned non-zero). No review PR was opened … Fix the push, then deliver again." No surface, and no server log line, retains WHAT git said. The stated redaction rationale is stale: `createGitHubAskpassEnv` (git-clone-auth.server.ts:42-76) supplies the PAT only through `GIT_ASKPASS`, never in argv or the remote URL, and `githubRemoteSanitizationArgs` scrubs legacy token-bearing origins — so the only token-shaped text stderr could carry is one the code could scrub by value. The same function already proves stderr is safe to read and classify.
confirmed.canon: planning/planning-artifacts/ux-design-specification.md:779 — "Error feedback must explain what failed, what remains true, and what the user can do next"; INTENT.md FR31/NFR14 (GitHub failures surfaced, delivery is the governed hand-off). The file's own sibling test (push-workspace.server.test.ts:262-281) rejects exactly this class one level up: "a process that was killed never 'returned' anything, and saying it did sends the reader hunting for a git error that was never printed."
confirmed.failure_scenario: A repo has a branch-protection rule (or a push ruleset, or a pre-receive hook) that rejects `vib-7`. The operator calls `deliver_for_review`; git exits non-zero with `remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed`. Viberr writes on VIB-7's timeline: "VIB-7's execution branch could not be pushed (git push returned non-zero). … Fix the push, then deliver again." The maintainer has a probe-verified credential, a workspace with commits, and a message that names no cause; the server log line carries only `{taskKey, branch}`. There is no path from Viberr to the word "protected" — the human must reproduce the push by hand outside the product, which is the make-or-break failure the UX spec names (reconstructing truth from outside the product).
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the RESIDUAL push_failed bucket in app/server/github/push-workspace.server.ts:391-402 (everything that is neither a timeout nor a non-fast-forward rejection — protected branch / push ruleset / pre-receive hook / 403 permission / DNS or network failure) collapses to the fixed string "git push returned non-zero", and git's stderr is retained nowhere: not on the timeline event (task-actions.server.ts:3429-3442), not in the server log line, not in any run log. A maintainer whose repo rejects vib-7 with "remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed" sees only "VIB-7's execution branch could not be pushed (git push returned non-zero) ... Fix the push, then deliver again" and must reproduce the push outside Viberr to learn the cause. The fix is a scrub-by-value stderr channel (the createLineRedactor pattern in run-sink.server.ts), NOT reading stderr raw — decisions.md:87 forbids secrets in files under projects/, in logs, and in error messages, and pushWorkspaceBranch never sanitizes a legacy token-bearing origin URL, so raw stderr can still carry a PAT. This is the push-side sibling of the already-open F19-6 (planning/discovery-2026-08-06-pass19/NOTES.md:29, clone-failure stderr dropped) and should be merged into it rather than filed as an independent defect.

The claim's premise that the redaction rationale is merely "stale" is overstated: credential-safe suppression of child-process stderr is a deliberate, documented codebase-wide pattern (app/server/tasks/git-clone-auth.server.ts:222-226 — "`Error.message`, `stderr`, and `cmd` are deliberately ignored because child process errors may echo command arguments or authentication diagnostics"; also agent-reply.server.ts:552-560). The accurate narrower finding is that the push-failure path is strictly less informative than the clone-failure path's own credential-safe model: cloneFailureLogDetails still classifies the failure (git_unavailable / clone_terminated / clone_failed) and surfaces the git exit code, whereas push_failed surfaces neither an exit code nor any classification beyond non-fast-forward, leaving "git push returned non-zero" as the only text a human ever sees. The fix implied is a classified cause plus exit code (and optionally scrub-by-value of the known token), not verbatim stderr.

confirmed.title: Two overlapping reconcile passes duplicate the divergence note and the watcher notifications
confirmed.claim: `reconcileTask` reads the task file at :168 and then awaits 2-4 GitHub round trips before writing at :457. The out-of-band transition guards (`prJustMerged`/`prJustClosed`/`prJustReopened`, :403-415) compare the LIVE PR state against the `fm.pr` snapshot captured before those awaits, and nothing serializes two passes over the same task: `reconcileProject` has no per-task or per-project lock, `runReconcile` (app/features/github/github-actions.server.ts:50) is not wrapped in `runSingleFlight` (unlike the rescan/rebuild sweeps), and `pollGithubReconcile` runs on its own 5-minute interval independent of the button. Both passes therefore see `fm.pr.state === "review"`, both compute `prJustMerged`, and both append the divergence timeline event (:488) and call `notifyTaskWatchers` (:528), which has no dedupe (task-actions.server.ts:267-282). The operator side is saved only by the unrelated lease in operator-run.server.ts. The function's own docstring claims "Idempotent", and the only idempotency test (github-reconciler.server.test.ts:454) runs the passes sequentially.
confirmed.canon: INTENT.md NFR16 — "idempotent external actions, retries never duplicate transitions/branches/PRs/events"; UX principle "Calm over chatter — suppress noise, duplication"; the module's own contract comment at :159-160 ("Idempotent: unchanged facts produce no file write").
confirmed.failure_scenario: A teammate merges VIB-7's PR on github.com. The 5-minute poller tick starts reconciling VIB-7 at 10:00:00 and is awaiting `getBranchCompare`; at 10:00:00.4 a maintainer clicks "Update status" on the GitHub page. Both passes read `pr.state: review` from task.md and both learn GitHub says merged. VIB-7's timeline then shows the identical "**Divergence:** PR #41 was merged on GitHub, but VIB-7 hasn't been accepted through Viberr…" note twice, and every admin/maintainer plus the task owner receives two identical inbox alerts for one event.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: reconcileTask's out-of-band transition guards are a read-then-write TOCTOU over the pre-await frontmatter snapshot (read :168, guards :403-415, write :457), and nothing serializes concurrent passes over the same task - reconcileProject/runReconcile take no lock and the always-on poller (boot.server.ts:307, boot pass + 5 min interval) is independent of the manual "Update status" action. Two overlapping passes that straddle an out-of-band PR merge/close/reopen therefore each append the divergence note (:488) and each fan out watcher notifications (:528), which have no dedupe at any layer. Corrections to the original framing: (1) NFR16 and the ":159-160 Idempotent" docstring are NOT contradicted - they speak to sequential retries, which genuinely hold and are tested (github-reconciler.server.test.ts:453 byte-stable second pass; the collision-note test near :430 runs three sequential passes and asserts exactly one note). The real gap is that concurrent overlap is simply uncovered by any guard or test; cite the "calm over chatter" UX principle and the missing single-flight, not a broken NFR16. (2) Blast radius is exactly two artifacts - the duplicate timeline note and duplicate inbox rows. The recommendation-withdrawal (:445-455) is an idempotent filter and autoInvokeOperator (:562) is coalesced by the operator lease, so neither duplicates. No state corruption (NFR13 is unaffected). (3) The most realistic trigger is not a sub-second coincidence with a poller tick but the BOOT poll pass - which exists specifically to surface divergences that landed while the process was down, spans seconds (20 tasks x 3-6 calls at concurrency 4) and coincides with a returning maintainer clicking "Update status" - or two maintainers clicking at once. Severity: LOW (user-visible duplication, no corruption).

Two narrowings to the claim as written. (1) The stated trigger (5-min poller tick coinciding with a click) is the least likely path: the overlap window is only the 2-4 GitHub round trips (~sub-second to a couple of seconds), so it is roughly a sub-1% chance per click. The reliably user-triggerable form is two concurrent sessions -- the disabled={busy} guard at github-view.tsx:479 is per-fetcher and per-page only, so two maintainers (or one maintainer in two tabs/windows) clicking "Update status" within the same second both reach the action and both race. (2) The duplication is not specific to the merged-divergence branch: acceptedClosedText (:389), closedButActive (:409) and prJustReopened (:415) are all derived from the same pre-await fm.pr snapshot and duplicate their timeline note plus inbox alert the same way.

confirmed.title: A scheduled operator re-run can still fire on a task that reached Done mid-tick
confirmed.claim: `fireDueSchedules` decides mootness from the PROJECTION row captured at the start of the tick (`row.archived`, `row.stage` from `tasksWithUnresolvedSchedules`, :228-240), then claims the occurrence inside `updateTaskFile` (:324-348) where the canonical frontmatter — including `parsed.frontmatter.stage` — is in hand under the file lock, but re-checks only `target.status`, never the stage. Each row costs an awaited locked write plus a reproject plus an audit insert, so the gap between the snapshot and the claim grows with the number of due schedules. `runOperator` has no terminal-stage guard of its own (no `isTerminalStage` reference in operator-run.server.ts), so a claim taken on a stale snapshot starts a real, unwatched operator turn on a closed task. This is the same hole P14-RV-03 closed for `archived`, left open for the stage dimension.
confirmed.canon: INTENT.md FR39 — a scheduled re-run "never fires on a terminal stage"; it is "the one capability that lets an agent act unwatched". decisions.md behavior rules: "Files are the only canonical business truth" — the projection must not decide what the file under lock already answers.
confirmed.failure_scenario: VIB-7 (stage Review) carries a schedule due 09:00. The 09:00 tick reads its candidate rows at 09:00:00.0, then works through three other due tasks. At 09:00:00.3 a maintainer accepts VIB-7's completion — task.md moves to `done`, the PR merges. At 09:00:00.9 the tick reaches VIB-7, sees `status: pending` in the file, and — because `isMoot` was computed from the pre-accept row — marks it `claimed`, writes "**Scheduled action starting:** … running the scheduled operator re-run for VIB-7", and enqueues a full operator turn against a merged, Done task with no human present. The human sees a fresh agent turn (and any recommendations it posts) on a task they just closed.
corrections:
Real, but LOW severity and one premise of the write-up is wrong.

Accurate claim: `fireDueSchedules` decides FR39 mootness from the tick's projection snapshot (`row.stage`, schedule.server.ts:309-312) and its in-lock re-check (:327) tests only `target.status`, never `parsed.frontmatter.stage` — the canonical value it already holds under the file lock. Because no writer cancels a schedule when a task reaches Done, an acceptance that lands between the tick's SELECT and that row's claim leaves the guard reading a stale stage, and the occurrence is claimed and enqueued into `runOperator`, which has no terminal-stage guard of its own. One line inside the existing `updateTaskFile` callback closes it.

Wrong premise to drop: "the same hole P14-RV-03 closed for `archived`". `row.archived` is equally snapshot-based — P14-RV-03 did not close a TOCTOU. The archived dimension survives because it is defended TWICE: `setTaskArchived` also flips pending/claimed schedules to `cancelled` in the file (task-actions.server.ts:4050-4055, explicitly called "belt-and-braces"), so the existing `target.status !== "pending"` re-check catches an archive that lands mid-tick. The Done dimension has no such second layer, which is precisely why the stale snapshot is load-bearing there.

Overstated: severity/likelihood. The exposure is the intra-tick window only — typically tens to hundreds of ms of awaited file writes — not a routinely hit path, and the stale-claim re-drive path self-corrects (a later tick re-SELECTs and sees `done` → retires with `skipped-done`). Also note a stage re-check at claim time would not cover the separate, larger claim→enqueue gap: `toRun` is drained after the loop in a detached IIFE that `await`s each `runOperator` sequentially (:390-458), so a task Done'd during a preceding run's drive is still not re-checked before its own run starts.

The defect is real but the practical trigger is wider than the sub-second mid-tick race the writeup leans on. Two reachable windows: (1) the claimed one — between tasksWithUnresolvedSchedules and the per-row claim write (tens to hundreds of ms, grows with the number of due rows); and (2) far more reachable — when an operator run is already in flight on the task, runOperator queues the scheduled trigger (operator-run.server.ts:717-726 -> queueOperatorTrigger:285) and drains it on lease release (releaseOperatorLease:366-372 / drainPendingAfterInFlight:383) with NO mootness re-check at all. That in-flight turn is frequently the one that calls accept_completion, so the schedule is claimed and finalized "fired" while the queued trigger later starts a real operator turn on a task that is now Done and merged. Note also that runOperator returns after startRun (it does not await the whole turn), so the "sequential toRun loop takes minutes" reading is wrong — the queued-trigger drain, not the toRun loop, is what stretches the window to a full operator turn.
